title: Daily drawdown limit (daily permitted loss)
value: 1-Step 3% | 2-Step Bright 4% | 2-Step Classic 5% | Original 2-Step 5% | Free $1K 3%
calculation_basis: Limit = (end-of-day highest of balance or equity at rollover) minus (daily % x ORIGINAL challenge size). Resets daily between 23:30 and 23:59 CET.
example: $100,000 2-Step Bright: you close the day at balance $102,000. Next day the floor is $102,000 - $4,000 = $98,000. Equity at or below $98,000 breaches the account.

title: Maximum drawdown - STATIC (2-Step plans)
value: 2-Step Bright 8% | 2-Step Classic 10% | Original 2-Step 10%
calculation_basis: Floor = initial balance x (1 - max%). Fixed from the start and never moves, regardless of profits.
example: $100,000 2-Step Classic: absolute floor $90,000 at all times. $100,000 2-Step Bright: absolute floor $92,000 at all times.

title: Maximum drawdown - TRAILING / high-water mark (1-Step, Free $1K)
value: 6% trailing, locks at breakeven once equity is +6%
calculation_basis: Floor = highest equity ever reached - 6% of original balance, but it never moves below initial balance - 6%, and once equity reaches initial + 6% the floor locks at the original balance and stops rising.
example: $1,000 account: start floor $940. Equity peaks at $1,040 -> floor rises to $980. The trade then reverses and closes at -$35, leaving balance $965 - below $980, so the account is breached even though it is still above the original $940 floor.

title: Floating (unrealised) P/L counts towards both limits
value: Equity = balance + floating P/L
calculation_basis: BrightFunded evaluates the higher of balance or equity, and equity includes open positions.
example: Balance $100,000 with an open -$3,000 position means equity $97,000 - already at the 3% daily floor on a $100,000 1-Step account.

title: Daily reset window (rollover)
value: 23:30 - 23:59 CET (daily loss reset); swap rollover 01:59 - 02:00 CET
calculation_basis: The daily loss counter resets during the rollover window. Times shift by +/-1 hour with European/US daylight-saving changes.
example: The FAQ notes market rollover spreads between 23:00 and 00:00 CET can trigger stop-losses on widened spreads rather than real price movement.

title: Historical daily-drawdown method (accounts bought before 22 Sep 2025, 11:00 CET)
value: 5% of challenge size, BALANCE based
calculation_basis: Old method: the daily permitted loss was 5% of the challenge size and was calculated from your BALANCE at rollover (not the higher of balance/equity).
example: $100,000 account, balance $100,000 with an open +$1,000 trade at rollover: old method still uses $100,000, so the floor is $95,000 (not $96,000).

title: Profit targets by phase
value: 1-Step 10% | 2-Step Bright 8% then 5% | 2-Step Classic 10% then 5% | Original 8% then 5% | Free $1K 10%
calculation_basis: Each phase target is a percentage of the account's initial balance. Phase 2 is only issued after Phase 1 is passed; credentials are sent automatically.
example: $50,000 2-Step Bright: Phase 1 needs +$4,000, Phase 2 needs +$2,500.

title: Minimum trading days
value: 5 trading days per phase (removable with the +15% 'No Minimum Trading Days' add-on)
calculation_basis: A day counts when at least one trade stays open for a minimum of 60 seconds - profit or loss makes no difference. Days need not be consecutive.
example: Twelve 20-second scalps on one day count as ONE trading day.

title: No time limit on the evaluation or verification
value: Unlimited days
calculation_basis: Both the Challenge and the Verification 'last for unlimited days from the date of activation'.
example: An account bought in January that has never been traded is suspended after 30 days and has a 6-month grace period to request reactivation.

title: Activate within 30 days of payment
value: 30 days
calculation_basis: Terms 6.3 / 6.10: if the Challenge or Verification is not activated within 30 days of payment or of receiving login data, access is automatically suspended; 6 months to request renewal or the service terminates without refund.
example: Buy on 1 March, never log in: suspended 31 March, permanently lost after 30 September with no refund.

title: What a breach actually does
value: Account invalidated / closed; challenge fee not refunded
calculation_basis: Official FAQ: breaching the rules makes the account automatically invalid, it cannot continue in the evaluation, and the initial fee is lost. You may buy a new challenge.
example: Touching the daily floor once on a $100K account ends that account; the fee is not returned unless you bought the fee-refund add-on and reached a payout.

title: Inactivity rule - 30 calendar days
value: 30 calendar days
calculation_basis: Policy effective 1 September 2025 and applied to all accounts including pre-existing ones. After your last closed trade you must place another trade that stays open at least 60 seconds within 30 days. Never-traded accounts must place a first trade within 30 days of assignment. Open positions keep the account active indefinitely, but pending orders do NOT count.
example: You hold an open EUR/USD position for 4 months - the account stays active. You have only pending limit orders - the countdown runs and the account deactivates after 30 days.

title: Single account policy - one profile per person
value: 1 email profile per person
calculation_basis: Terms 4.1. Detection uses names, personal data, IP addresses, device fingerprints, payment patterns, KYC submissions and other methods.
example: Buying five $100K challenges on one profile is allowed. Creating a second login to get a 'new customer' promo code is not.

title: Maximum funded capital per trader: $400,000
value: $400,000 funded (unlimited during the challenge stage)
calculation_basis: Terms 6.14 and the official FAQ. Extra passed Phase 2 accounts above the cap are placed on hold until a funded account is breached.
example: Two $200K funded accounts, or four $100K funded accounts, is the maximum. A fifth $100K funded account waits on hold.

title: Account merging (funded stage only)
calculation_basis: Only funded accounts, only two accounts, identical add-ons (same platform, same split, same payout frequency), and both accounts must be 'clean' (no trades) at the moment of the request. Irreversible.
example: Two untouched $50K funded accounts with identical add-ons can become one $100K funded account.

title: News trading - 10-minute blackout on FUNDED accounts only
value: No opening or closing trades 5 minutes before to 5 minutes after a high-impact release
calculation_basis: Effective 9 May 2024. During the 10-minute window you may not open, close, or have SL/TP/buy-stop/sell-stop orders triggered on targeted instruments. Profit made on a violating trade is deducted; losses are NOT compensated. Explicitly a SOFT breach - the account is not terminated.
example: A trade held 48+ hours whose take-profit fills during the 10-minute window is exempt - the profit is kept.

title: Which news events are targeted
value: High-impact ('red folder') events; BrightFunded links Forex Factory as the reference calendar
calculation_basis: The rule applies to 'targeted instruments' only; you may trade non-targeted instruments normally during the window.
example: An FOMC release targets USD pairs; trading an unrelated exotic during the same window is generally allowed.

title: Expert Advisors (EAs) / trading bots
value: Allowed with conditions
calculation_basis: EAs are permitted but must respect the daily and total loss limits. API and automated trading are NOT supported on DXtrade. Compatibility of third-party EAs is not guaranteed.
example: A standard MT5 grid-free EA is fine; an HFT bot placing and cancelling orders in milliseconds is not.

title: Copy trading / signal trading
value: Allowed only between accounts you own
calculation_basis: Copying between BrightFunded accounts, other evaluation firms, or retail brokerage accounts is allowed if every account belongs to the same person. Copying between accounts of different owners - including relatives, family or friends - is prohibited, as is trading on community signals. Detection compares opening price, closing price, trade size, size ratio and symbols.
example: Copying your own retail account into your BrightFunded account: allowed. Following a paid Telegram signal group: prohibited.

title: Hedging across accounts, platforms or prop firms
value: First detection = soft breach (one-time warning); repeat = hard breach
calculation_basis: Effective 13 August 2024. Prohibited: the same instrument hedged across two BrightFunded accounts, across two platforms on the same profile, across different prop firms, or via a copier/EA. First detection closes all open trades in the involved accounts and issues a one-time warning; a second detection permanently breaches them. The one-time warning only applies if a single trade is involved on each side - two or more offsetting trades is an immediate hard breach.
example: Account A buys 1 lot EUR/USD while Account B sells 1 lot EUR/USD = inter-account hedging. Account A holding both a buy and a sell on EUR/USD = allowed.

title: Prohibited strategy list (grid, HFT, tick scalping, arbitrage, overleveraging)
value: Grid trading, arbitrage, tick scalping, HFT, overleveraging, overexposure, one-sided bets (averaging down), account rolling - all forbidden
calculation_basis: Help Centre 'Which strategies are prohibited' plus Terms 5.4-5.5. The Terms also forbid gap trading when significant news or macro events are due, and exploiting service errors, price-feed delays, or using a slower external data feed.
example: Continuously averaging down a losing long position is named as 'one-sided bets' and is prohibited. Placing a buy/sell ladder at fixed intervals is named as grid trading and is prohibited.

title: Minimum holding time and scalping
value: No formal minimum holding time, but tick scalping is not allowed
calculation_basis: Official FAQ: no minimum holding time is enforced; tick scalping is not allowed and the firm recommends avoiding closing too many trades in very short periods.
example: Dozens of sub-second entries per hour can be treated as tick scalping even though no numeric limit is published.

title: Weekend and overnight holding
value: Allowed
calculation_basis: Positions may be held over the weekend. Crypto instruments can be traded at weekends when the instrument is open.
example: A forex position held through Wednesday night is charged triple swap.

title: VPN, VPS and IP addresses
value: Allowed
calculation_basis: Using a VPN/VPS or a different IP while travelling is permitted. What is prohibited is anybody other than the account owner using or trading the account.
example: Trading from a VPS in London while you live in Warsaw is fine. Letting a friend trade your account is not.

title: Stop-loss requirement
value: Not mandatory
calculation_basis: Official FAQ: a stop-loss is not mandatory but is strongly recommended.
example: An unprotected position on gold can move 3% of a $100K account in minutes during a news release.

title: First payout timing
value: 30 days after the first trade on the funded account
calculation_basis: Official reward-split article: you can request your first reward split 30 days after placing your first trade on the funded account.
example: First funded trade on 1 March -> first eligible payout request 31 March.

title: Payout frequency after the first payout
value: Bi-weekly (14 days) by default; weekly (7 days) with the +25% add-on
calculation_basis: Default cycle is bi-weekly. The checkout 'Weekly Payouts' add-on costs +25% of the challenge fee; 'Bi-Weekly Payouts' is listed at +15%, so verify whether you are already getting 14 days for free before paying for it.
example: Without add-ons you can request a payout roughly every 14 days after the first one.

title: Profit split
value: 80% default, 90% with the +20% add-on, 90% after the 1st scale-up, 100% from the 3rd scale-up
calculation_basis: Reward-split article plus the scaling-plan page. The firm also markets 'up to 90%' on plan pages and 'up to 100%' in the comparison table - both are reachable, but only via add-on or scaling.
example: $10,000 of simulated profit at the default split pays $8,000; with the 90% add-on it pays $9,000.

title: Minimum payout amount
value: None stated - 'even $0.01' can be requested
calculation_basis: Official reward-split article: there is no minimum reward. This CONFLICTS with the free-$1K page, which advertises a first payout of $40 (5% profit) and with the free-$1K vs $100K comparison showing a 'Minimum $4,000 Payout' for the $100K challenge.
example: On a $100,000 challenge the website implies the first payout is $4,000 (5% of $100,000 x 80%).

title: Payout fees
value: BrightFunded charges none; third-party processor/network fees typically $5-$50
calculation_basis: Official help article: no additional fees are charged by the firm; blockchain gas and payment-provider charges are deducted by third parties and 'in very rare cases' can exceed $5-$50. Currency conversion is at real-time partner rates.
example: A $1,000 payout can arrive as roughly $950-$995 depending on network and provider fees.

title: Payout processing time
value: Maximum 1 day (24 hours) after request; the site advertises an average of about 17 hours
calculation_basis: Help article: 'it will take a maximum of 1 day to be processed'. The marketing claim '24-Hour Guaranteed Payouts' is not published as a contractual guarantee.
example: Request on Monday morning, funds processed by Tuesday; bank settlement can take several additional business days.

title: Payout methods and currencies
value: USDC on ERC-20, or bank transfer in EUR
calculation_basis: Help centre. Changing your wallet address requires a video verification showing your dashboard, the payout section and the new USDC ERC-20 address in one continuous recording.
example: A trader wanting USD must use USDC and convert.

title: Consistency rule
value: NOT enforced (none)
calculation_basis: Official FAQ and a dedicated help article both state that BrightFunded does not currently enforce a consistency rule: no requirement to spread profits across days or trades and no fixed position size.
example: Making your entire 10% on a single day does not, by itself, prevent a payout request.

title: Profit cap / maximum withdrawal
value: None
calculation_basis: Official FAQ: 'BrightFunded does not have a profit cap - your earnings have no per-cycle withdrawal limit'.
example: A $50,000 profit cycle on a $200K account is payable in full at your split.

title: KYC / identity verification
value: Government ID + proof of address, via SumSub
calculation_basis: KYC is mandatory before the funded account is issued and before payouts. Performed by SumSub to AML standards. KYB (business verification) is not required.
example: Independent reviews report KYC and credential delays as a recurring complaint, so allow for the 1-4 day window before planning payouts.

title: Trading commissions
value: Forex $3 per lot | Indices $0 | Crypto 0.024% of volume (0.012% per side) | Commodities 0.0010% of volume
calculation_basis: Official help article. Commissions apply identically in the challenge and the funded stage because the firm mirrors trades onto its own corporate live accounts.
example: A 5-lot EUR/USD round trip costs $15 in commission regardless of profit or loss.

title: Leverage by asset class
value: Forex 1:100 | Gold & commodities 1:40 | Indices 1:20 | Crypto 1:5
calculation_basis: Official help article. Identical leverage in the challenge and funded stages.
example: On a $100,000 account: $10,000,000 forex notional, $4,000,000 metals, $2,000,000 indices, $500,000 crypto.

title: Swap / rollover fees
value: Charged at 01:59-02:00 CET; 3x on Wednesday (FX & commodities) and Friday (indices) unless swap-free
calculation_basis: Official help article. Swap-free requires the +10% checkout add-on. Swap fees displayed in pips on the platform.
example: A position held through Wednesday night is charged triple the normal overnight swap.

title: Trading platforms
value: MetaTrader 5, cTrader, DXtrade
calculation_basis: Official help article. MT5 unavailable to US/UAE citizens or residents and restricted countries; cTrader unavailable to US citizens/residents. DXtrade does not support API or automated trading.
example: A US-based trader cannot use MT5 or cTrader and must use DXtrade.

title: Tradable instruments
value: 46 forex pairs listed; 48 crypto pairs; indices; metals and energy commodities
calculation_basis: The trading-instruments page lists 46 forex symbols in its HTML; the crypto help article lists 48 crypto pairs. Indices and commodities are described but the full symbol list is rendered dynamically and could not be fully extracted.
example: Confirmed symbols include EUR/USD, GBP/USD, XAU/USD, XAG/USD, WTI/USD, BRN/USD, NGC/USD, US100.cash, US500.cash, US30.cash, JPN225.cash and BTC/USD.

title: Refund policy
value: Refund if NO trade was placed and the purchase is under 30 days old
calculation_basis: Help article: contact support via live chat; refund processed within 48 hours and arrives in 3-10 business days. Terms 3.3: no refunds if you cancel the client section, stop using the service, fail the conditions or breach the terms.
example: Bought 10 days ago, never logged in: refundable. Placed one trade: not refundable.

title: 100% challenge fee refund (add-on) and its forfeiture condition
value: +10% of challenge fee; refunded with the first payout
calculation_basis: Terms 7.7(b): the challenge fee is refunded only if the add-on was purchased, and it is included in the first performance-reward disbursement. If the funded account is later suspended, no further refund is issued.
example: A $100K 2-Step Classic at EUR 497 with the add-on (+10% = 497) returns EUR 497 with your first payout.

title: Scaling plan
value: +30% account size every 4 months; 90% split after scale-up 1; 100% from scale-up 3; no upper limit
calculation_basis: Requirements: 4-month consecutive review window from the first trade; profitable in at least 2 of the 4 months; at least 10% total profit across the window; at least 2 completed payouts; balance at breakeven or better at the moment of scaling. Must be requested from support - it is not automatic.
example: A $100,000 funded account that meets the conditions becomes $130,000; after the third scale-up the split is 100%.

title: 15% evaluation profit reward
value: 15% of Phase 1 + Phase 2 profit, credited to your next funded account
calculation_basis: Effective 3 January 2026. Available only on PAID challenge accounts (not the free $1K). Requires reaching 10% growth on the funded account and receiving a payout. One article says you must contact support to have it applied; another describes it as issued automatically - unresolved.
example: $100,000 account, $13,000 total evaluation profit -> bonus $1,950 -> next funded account starts at $101,950.

title: Trade2Earn loyalty tokens
value: 0.2 tokens per $100,000 traded (FX, indices, commodities); 0.2 tokens per $20,000 traded (crypto)
calculation_basis: Official help article. Tokens accrue on every trade regardless of profit or loss, in both challenge and funded phases, and can be redeemed for perks such as extra drawdown, lower profit targets, fee refunds and discounts.
example: Trading $1,000,000 of forex volume earns 2 tokens.

title: Chargeback policy and enforcement
value: Disputing a payment can terminate services
calculation_basis: Terms 3.4 covers 'unjustifiable complaints' and the Help Centre has a dedicated Chargeback Policy & Enforcement article. The firm may act if a chargeback or payment dispute is filed without first attempting resolution.
example: Filing a card chargeback without contacting support is treated as a breach-level event.

title: Risk team discretion and temporary risk measures
value: Firm may reduce leverage to 1:5, cut daily drawdown, limit position size or impose other restrictions
calculation_basis: Terms 5.8 allows the firm to remove transactions, cancel services, terminate the agreement, reduce leverage to 1:5, or impose additional trading restrictions. The funded-account help article confirms 'temporary risk measures may be applied' in rare cases where a strategy is judged higher risk.
example: A trader using a high-volume news strategy may have the daily limit reduced mid-account.

title: Performance rewards are discretionary
value: Rewards are 'discretionary and do not constitute a guaranteed right or entitlement'
calculation_basis: Terms 6.19 and 7.8. Funded Trader Program admission is at the firm's sole discretion (7.2, 7.5).
example: A rejected payout can be defended by the firm on the basis of clauses 6.19 / 7.8 even where no explicit rule was broken.

title: Free $1K Challenge eligibility
value: One per user; no other active accounts; restricted countries excluded; limited claims per country per day
calculation_basis: Help article. Requires verified email (no + alias, no disposable domain), a verified phone number (one number per account) and a completed survey. Multiple free accounts are not allowed.
example: Holding an active paid challenge disqualifies you from claiming the free $1K until that account is closed.

title: Restricted countries
value: Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Vietnam (Terms) + Pakistan (Help Centre)
calculation_basis: Terms section 2 lists Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria and Vietnam. The Help Centre adds Pakistan but says existing Pakistani accounts may continue trading. MT5 is additionally unavailable to US and UAE residents/citizens.
example: A trader resident in Vietnam cannot register; a trader resident in Pakistan is blocked by the Help Centre list but not by the Terms.

title: Can I register as a company?
value: Yes - invoices and payouts can be in the company name
calculation_basis: Official FAQ: register as an individual using the company address, then add business information in the profile. Invoices are issued in the company name and payouts can go to the company bank account. No KYB process.
example: A trading company can have the invoice and payout in its own name without a KYB review.
